tasks.title: Keep Pod tab titles visible while the fork-error alert is shown
acceptance: C1 cause named: the report names the cause of the Pod tab titles collapsing while the fork-error alert is shown, at `file:line` in the code at base 74e79ff, and says how the change removes it. (Architect's reading, to be confirmed or refuted by the implementer: in the `.chrome` flex row, `PodsChrome.module.css:13-16` gives the Pod bar panel `flex: 1 1 auto`, while the fork-error row `.dismissible` (`:32-36`) keeps the default `flex: 0 1 auto` and so a flex basis of the message's full one-line width; the two shrink in proportion to their bases, so a long message takes width from the bar, whose `.title` spans (`PodBar.module.css:106-112`, `overflow: hidden`, inside `min-width: 0` tabs) collapse first.)

C2 the fix keeps each Pod tab title at the width it has without an alert while the fork-error alert is shown (amended A1, E3: the title widths are the requirement; the `pod-bar` element's own width may change, and O17 records it without scoring it). The scored evidence is the driver's O17 in T2 (contract section C); this task's evidence is C3's test plus the report's statement of which declarations make the title widths independent of the alert's message length.

C3 regression test (encodes test discipline, Coverage: a bug fix arrives with the test that reproduces it, and a test is shown able to fail). A test in the node environment reads the changed stylesheet(s) as text, after the `#?raw` pattern of `src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.styles.test.ts:16`, in `fork-error-layout.styles.test.ts` or an owned `*.styles.test.ts`, and asserts the declarations C2's statement names. A stylesheet-text test is the project's route for layout defects that jsdom cannot lay out (`fork-ui-regression.styles.test.ts:7-13`). Demonstrated discrimination: the report names one `file:line` of the fix, reverts that one declaration, runs `npx vitest run <that test file>` and quotes the failure, then restores it and quotes the passing run. The window is reported (what was reverted, the command run under it, that it was restored).

C4 the alert's text is not painted outside the Pod-bar row. The bar row is 38px (`--oc-pod-bar-height`, `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:189`); a message that no longer takes width from the bar wraps onto more lines, so the fix bounds the alert's painted text to the row (decided at Gate 2, E1: the visible text is clamped to the row). The scored evidence is the driver's O18 in T2; this task's report states the declaration(s) that bound it, and C3's test asserts them.

C5 full message still available (decided at Gate 2, E1): the fork-error alert element carries a `title` equal to main's message, verbatim. A jsdom test in `src/renderer/src/__tests__/pod-fork.e2e.test.tsx` asserts `alert.getAttribute('title')` equals the failure message; at base no `title` is set on the alert (`PodsChrome.tsx:291-293`), and the report shows the test failing before the change (red step: command and output).

C6 DOM hooks kept (contract section A, consumed by T2): the alert's message is a direct text-node child of the `role="alert"` element. Preserved, newly tested: a jsdom test in `pod-fork.e2e.test.tsx` asserts that the alert's `firstChild` is a `Text` node whose `data` equals the failure message. Its discrimination is shown by wrapping `{forkError}` in a `<span>` at `PodsChrome.tsx:292`, running `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/pod-fork.e2e.test.tsx`, quoting the failure, and restoring. The existing tests at `pod-fork.e2e.test.tsx:359-395` (native button, aria-hidden glyph, button outside the alert with alert text exactly main's message, click removes the alert) still pass unmodified.

C7 O10's fix preserved: `fork-ui-regression.styles.test.ts` keeps its four `it` blocks with their assertions unweakened (in particular `.dismissible`'s `align-items` is `['flex-start']`, `:45`), and passes.

C8 no token change: `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css` is not in this task's `owns`; a fix that needs a new or changed token is reported as an escalation, with no partial fix (as in the prior session's contract I5). Every `var(--oc-*)` the changed stylesheets use is in the frozen TOKENS map, which `PodsChrome.styles.test.ts:48-54` and the matching PodBar test check.

C9 encodes frontend discipline, Accessibility floor (keyboard reachable; focus visible and predictable): `Dismiss fork error` stays a native `button` outside the alert, and the chrome stays programmatically focusable: `grep -c 'tabIndex={-1}' src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.tsx` prints 1 (base prints 1, measured at 74e79ff).

C10 encodes the project frontend fragment (indexed access under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`): no added line in an owned production file uses a non-null assertion `!` or an `as` cast as the guard for an indexed or destructured value.
C11 no session path: `grep -c '\.sir/'` over each owned file prints 0 (each existing owned file prints 0 at base 74e79ff).
C12 `npm run typecheck` in the worktree exits 0 at this task's tip.

C13 `npm test` in the worktree exits 0 at this task's tip, 0 failed files and 0 failed tests; the report gives the passed file and test counts (base: 157 files / 2544 tests, the orchestrator's probe).
